handbookNote: Virginia Real Estate Broker license exam. Genuinely NEW track -- Virginia previously had no broker-tier track on this site, only va_re_salesperson. Exam vendor: PSI Services LLC, under contract with the Virginia Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation (DPOR) Real Estate Board. PRIMARY-CONFIRMED by directly downloading and reading (via the Read tool against a raw-downloaded PDF, after the display_bulletin.jsp redirect chain required navigating PSI's test-taker SPA via browser automation to find the real content API endpoint) PSI's own official Virginia Real Estate Candidate Information Bulletin (copyright 2026, last revised 2/18/2026). This single 18-page document supplied BOTH the exam mechanics AND the full real content outline for both the National and Virginia State portions -- not a third-party test-prep summary. Exam Summary Table, quoted directly from the bulletin: Broker exam = 125 total items across two SEPARATELY-SCORED, separately-timed portions -- National (75 items/80 points possible, 105 min) and Virginia State (50 items/50 points, 55 min), combined 160-minute time limit. A footnote states 'National broker exams include questions that are scored up to two points,' disclosed here rather than silently flattened. Passing score, quoted directly from the bulletin's own Score Reporting table: National Portion 60 (of 80 points, =75%), State Portion 38 (of 50, =76%) -- both portions must be passed independently. This site's track_registry schema models one combined row rather than two separately-scored portions, so the DB row records combined totals (125 questions, 9600s/160min duration, 75% pass, min_correct=94 as the nearest whole-item rounding of 125 x 0.75) -- the real two-portion, two-timer, separately-scored structure is disclosed in the track's own description/mechanicsNote copy instead. A small number of 1-10 unscored experimental items (~10% of the exam) may also appear, counted against exam time. CONTENT OUTLINE -- National portion percentages, quoted verbatim from the bulletin (Broker column, summing to exactly 100% of the 75-item national portion, independently re-verified by hand this session): Property Ownership 10%, Land Use Controls 5%, Valuation 8%, Financing 9%, Contracts 19% (the largest single national topic), Agency 13%, Property Disclosures 7%, Property Management 5% (has Broker-only sub-items on trust-fund handling/maintenance/reporting responsibility), Transfer of Title 6%, Practice of Real Estate 12% (has a Broker-only Supervisory Responsibilities sub-section), Real Estate Calculations 6%. NOTABLE: these percentages are IDENTICAL to Tennessee's own PSI-published national-portion percentages for the Broker exam (see tn_re_broker.json) -- confirms PSI uses one shared multi-state 'National Portion' content-outline template for real estate broker exams, with only the State-specific portion varying meaningfully by state. Virginia State portion, quoted verbatim as item counts (of the 50-item state portion, Broker column, summing to the full 50): Licensing 13 items (Qualifications/Requirements including Broker's Supervisory Requirements and Disciplinary Procedures/Sanctions, Inspection of Records and Audits, license types and activities requiring a license, License Maintenance including post-license/continuing education/license transfer); Escrow Accounts 7 items; Disclosure Requirements 7 items (Property Disclosure incl. Chesapeake Bay Act, Aircraft Noise/Crash Disclosure, Septic Disclosure, Megan's Law, Stigmatized Properties, HOA/POA disclosures, Advertising Rules); Agency Definitions and Relationships 12 items (Broker-Salesperson Relationships and Compensation, Limited Service, Disclosure of Agency, agency duties, Designated and Dual Agency, Unrepresented parties); Virginia Fair Housing Law and Regulations 6 items; Specific Acts Pertaining to Real Estate Practice 5 items (Virginia Condominium Act and Regulations, Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, Virginia Common Interest Communities Act -- Broker only, Virginia Underground Utility Damage Prevention Act, Virginia Property Owner's Association Act). This bank's bucket sizing is directly proportional to these real, PSI-published weights (each national bucket's target count scaled off its published % of the 75-item national portion; each Virginia bucket's target count scaled off its published item-count out of the 50-item state portion), not an even split -- actual per-bucket counts were then set by each drafting pass to whatever its real, verifiable source material actually supported. Real Virginia statute/regulation facts independently verified this session via law.lis.virginia.gov (Virginia's official law site) -- Va. Code Title 54.1, Chapter 21 (Real Estate License Laws, e.g. §§ 54.1-2106.1, 54.1-2106.2, 54.1-2108, 54.1-2108.1, 54.1-2108.2, 54.1-2110.1, 54.1-2130 through 54.1-2146, 54.1-2139.1, 54.1-2146); 18VAC135-20 (Virginia Real Estate Board Regulations, e.g. 18VAC135-20-70, 101, 155, 165, 170, 181, 185, 220, 225, 240, 260, 270, 280, 300, 310, 330); Va. Code Title 36, Chapter 5.1 (Virginia Fair Housing Law, §§ 36-96.1 through 36-96.20); Virginia Condominium Act (Va. Code Title 55.1, Chapter 19, § 55.1-1900 et seq.); Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (§ 55.1-1200 et seq.); Virginia Common Interest Communities Act (§ 54.1-2345 et seq.); Virginia Underground Utility Damage Prevention Act (§ 56-265.15 et seq.); Virginia Property Owners' Association Act (§ 55.1-1800 et seq.). NOTABLE real-law finding from this build: the old separate Condominium Act resale-certificate sections (former §§ 55.1-1988-1995) and POA Act disclosure-packet sections (former §§ 55.1-1808-1814) were REPEALED effective July 1, 2023 and consolidated into a new unified Resale Disclosure Act (Va. Code Title 55.1, Chapter 23.1, § 55.1-2307 et seq.) that now governs resale certificates for both condos and POAs -- this bank uses the current, correct post-2023 citations, not the outdated pre-2023 ones a less careful build might have used. Standard national real-estate/appraisal/finance/contract-law/math content not tied to a Virginia-specific statute (property ownership, land use theory, valuation approaches and calculations, agency doctrine, financing/RESPA/TILA/TRID/ECOA, deed types, title/closing mechanics, federal fair housing/ADA/antitrust) is sourced to 'national real estate [contract/agency/practice] law principles' framing throughout, consistent with this project's standard for generic/national content never presented as a pinpoint state citation. Price set at $29.99 (2999 cents) to match this project's standardized Real Estate Broker track rate (nj_re_broker.json, ny_re_broker.json, tn_re_broker.json, ga_re_broker.json, pa_re_broker.json, ca_re_broker.json, fl_re_broker.json, oh_re_broker.json, tx_re_broker.json, mi_re_broker.json). This bank was drafted across six parallel content-authoring passes grouped by real content-outline topic clusters, each pass instructed to draft every question with the correct answer as choice_a, then deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_va_re_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation across all 16 bucket files combined, in file order). Three genuine cross-bucket near-duplicates were found and manually removed before rotation (Licensing and Escrow Accounts buckets, drafted by different agents, both independently cited the same 18VAC135-20-185/260 provisions with near-identical question framing and identical answers on three separate points -- three-year records-retention period, the escrow-check-payable-to-licensee prohibition, and the required contents of financial records -- caught by comparing shared source_note citations across all 16 files, since the automated per-topic dedup in build-track-batch.js cannot catch a duplicate that spans two different topic strings; all three retained copies live in Escrow Accounts, the more natural topical home, with the Licensing duplicates deleted). All remaining draft questions passed an automated schema/weight-range/distinct-choice validation pass, and were additionally run through this project's standard Jaccard-similarity dedup check (scripts/build-track-batch.js) at build time to remove any further exact or near-duplicate items before loading. A stray leftover from an earlier aborted single-fork build attempt of this same track (a `_buckets/` directory with one incompatible .js-module-format file and a `_build_all.js` orchestration script, from before the parallel-drafting-agent model was adopted) was found in the target directory and discarded as stale, incompatible debris before this build -- none of its content was reused. POST-BUILD CORRECTION (2026-09-02): discovered this build's six drafting passes had been given a per-bucket target computed from a fixed item-count-times-multiplier formula, and 3 of the resulting buckets (Property Management, Property Disclosures, Specific Acts Pertaining to Real Estate Practice) landed suspiciously exactly on that target -- clear anchoring, not a genuine content ceiling. Standing policy corrected project-wide: pool ratios are a floor to check after drafting, never a target given to a drafting agent. Ran a full backfill: de-rotated all 16 files back to the choice_a-correct convention, relaunched the 3 flagged topics with no ceiling (added 14/17/17 respectively), re-checked cross-bucket dedup (2 new near-duplicates found and resolved the same way as the original 3 -- Licensing vs. Escrow Accounts, same 18VAC135-20-185/260 citations, kept in Escrow Accounts), re-rotated the full set, and rebuilt. FINAL: 580 questions (up from 534) -- a 4.64:1 pool ratio, fully reloaded into D1 (534 old rows deleted, 580 new rows inserted, verified by count).
